Re: Mouse In The Kitchen

MOUSE IN THE KITCHEN, Anglo-Irish Jig in A Major. Written by Colin Farrell. Born in Manchester, England to Irish parents, Colin now lives in Florida. He wrote this tune while studying for a Master’s Degree in Irish Music at The University of Limerick. A mouse appeared in the kitchen as he was writing this tune.
His acting in ‘Banshees of Inisherin,’ ‘The Lobster,’ and ‘Saving Mrs. Banks’ (and more) cannot be understated as anything other than outstanding. I am a huge fan!

↳ Posted by skylos on April 8th, 2026.

Jim Ward jig/Mouse in the Kitchen name curiosity

Recently while looking at the “Popular Tunes” I saw a jig named “Jim Ward”. I assumed it was probably “Jimmy Ward’s Jig” but when I played the first setting it was not. However, it was really familiar and I realized it is a tune that we have recently been playing which we know as “Mouse in the Kitchen”. Then, duh, I noticed that under the tune name it was indeed also known as “Mouse in the Kitchen” and “Mouse in the Cupboard”.

I got curious and tried a little internet surfing to try to determine if the composer originally called it “Jim Ward” and the ‘folk process’ somehow managed to come up with “Mouse in the Kitchen” but searches for “Jim Ward Jig” always resulted in references to the tune I know as “Jimmy’s Wards”, and searches for “Mouse in the Kitchen” always seemed to come up with a discussion of how the tune was written by Colin Farrell. So, I’m curious. Did Colin name it “Jim Ward”?

Ah, the ’folk process”. I’m used to many tunes having many names, and many different tunes often having the same name. Part of the charm of the tradition I guess. This one just seemed odd since it is a relatively recently composed tune named so similarly to an old session standard.

To add an extra bit of confusion, the Session shows 15 video’s for “Jim Ward” jig, and only the first four are the tune I know as “Mouse in the Kitchen”, and the rest are all of the tune I know as “Jimmy Ward’s Jig”. (By the way, I’m not criticizing that new Session feature with the videos – I find that feature really useful!!)

↳ Posted by flyrodandbrush on June 13th, 2026.
